candidates.transition_rationale: state1536 transitions to 15 (request-active) under mode logic that is intertwined with write-request conditions; state2002 (r_pipe_req) is set by write strobe and address matching, and the pipe request flag is expected to be active when the DSPI enters request-active mode.
candidates.why_consistent_with_reachable_samples: The only sample with state1536=15 also has state2002=1; no sample contradicts this implication.
candidates.why_nontrivial: Links a specific mode value to a control flag, not a bitwidth tautology.

candidates.transition_rationale: Active mode (10) is entered when the bus is accessed under specific conditions. The transition logic shows state1536 depends on ~state79 and ~state790 during the transition, but once in mode 10 either the config mode (state79) or the write stall (state790) becomes asserted, as seen in the dependencies.
candidates.why_consistent_with_reachable_samples: Sample with state1536=10 and state79=1 makes the consequent true; the other sample with state1536=10 and state790=1 also makes it true. In all other samples state1536≠10, so the implication holds vacuously.
candidates.why_nontrivial: Requires at least one of two distinct control signals to be true when in a specific mode—a non-obvious invariant.

candidates.transition_rationale: IDLE mode (0) is the reset state. In IDLE, either the high-speed configuration (state1558) is active or the write-bus stall (state790) is asserted, reflecting the system’s behaviour that a stall or speed config is set when no DSPI transaction is ongoing.
candidates.why_consistent_with_reachable_samples: Sample4 has state1536=0 and state1558=1; Sample5 has state1536=0 and state790=1. Both satisfy the consequent. Other samples have state1536≠0, so the implication is vacuously true.
candidates.why_nontrivial: Asserts a disjunction constraint on two independent control bits during IDLE—nontrivial because IDLE could otherwise be consistent with many combinations.
